defects: Restricts to 𝕜 = ℂ only, whereas gold is stated for general RCLike 𝕜 (covers ℝ and ℂ)

Requires a linear isometric equivalence f : E ≃ₗᵢ F (hence bijective, and both E and F finite-dimensional) instead of a general linear isometry f : U →ₗᵢ V (only injective, target V need not be finite-dimensional) as in gold

Uses arbitrary bases basis_E, basis_F with no orthonormality requirement, whereas the informal/gold notion of norm-determinant is defined via orthonormal bases; using arbitrary bases changes the mathematical content

States mere existence of some pair of bases making |det| = 1 rather than asserting a canonically-defined invariant (normDet) equals 1 for the (orthonormal) basis-independent quantity; since basis_F can be chosen as the image of basis_E under f, the matrix becomes the identity and the claim becomes trivially true, not capturing the substantive content of the gold theorem
Drops the W type variable/section context (minor, unused in gold theorem itself)
